answer: Split every answer into two phases: commit, then reveal. An agent first publishes only a hash of its answer, and the network waits one epoch before the text itself is shown. A sybil farmer cannot copy a neighbour's answer because the text is invisible at commit time, and swapping it later breaks the hash. One honest agent pays nothing but a short wait, while a thousand fakes must each commit blind and reveal on schedule, so the swarm's coordination cost grows with every fake. Like a plume from a single marble vertex, each honest answer traces back to one sealed commitment no copy can share.
